goal_summary: Bounded source investigation and primary-literature curation of five uncurated IMA-approved critical-element mineral species from the September 2026 IMA-CNMNC Master List with open-access type descriptions in European Journal of Mineralogy (volumes 32, 36, and 38): pilanesbergite (IMA:2023-007), luxembourgite (IMA:2018-154), tancaite-ce (IMA:2009-097), argentotennantite-fe (IMA:2023-126), and badengzhuite (IMA:2019-076).

curated_sources_and_records.name: Pilanesbergite
curated_sources_and_records.type_locality: Green foyaite (nepheline syenite) in a river gulley near the southern margin of the Pilanesberg Alkaline Complex (25.3463° S, 27.0658° E), North West Province, South Africa
type_specimens: Cotype KNR 44406 (Natural History Museum, University of Oslo, Norway; sample used for EPMA, SCXRD structural refinement, and petrographic description)
Cotype 21980 (Laboratoire de Minéralogie, University of Liège, Belgium; sample used for PXRD, optical properties, and density measurement)

primary_source.citation: Dal Bo F, Friis H, Elburg MA, Hatert F, Andersen T (2024) Pilanesbergite: a new rock-forming mineral occurring in nepheline syenite from the Pilanesberg Alkaline Complex, South Africa. European Journal of Mineralogy 36:73-85

primary_source_discrepancies_documented: Figure 2 (p. 76) labels pilanesbergite with the mineral symbol 'Pbt', whereas the September 2026 IMA-CNMNC Master List (p. 173) assigns the symbol 'Pbg'.
Abstract (p. 73) and Section 3 (p. 74) report Dcalc = 3.40 g/cm3 alongside Dmeas = 3.47 g/cm3, whereas Table 3 (p. 79) reports Calculated density = 3.49 g/cm3.

Table 1 (p. 77) prints the EPMA mean oxide/halogen total (n = 15 analyses, 5 um beam) as 102.13 wt% and 99.80 wt% after -O=F (2.33 wt%), whereas the arithmetic sum of the 14 printed mean constituent values (SiO2 32.28 + Al2O3 0.03 + TiO2 18.33 + ZrO2 2.95 + FeO 9.70 + MnO 4.96 + MgO 0.49 + CaO 16.87 + Na2O 9.43 + K2O 0.01 + SrO 0.18 + Nb2O5 1.36 + Ce2O3 0.02 + F 5.54) is 102.15 wt% and 99.82 wt% after -O=F.
Section 6.1 (p. 77) refers to the anionic sites as 'The W1 (O4) and W2 (F) sites', whereas Tables 4 (p. 80) and 7 (p. 81) identify W1 as O8 (W1).
Table 4 (p. 80) prints Ueq for site X3 (Fe) as '0.349(4)' Å2, a decimal-place typographical error relative to X1 (Ti) = 0.00650(5), X2 (Ca) = 0.00926(7), and X4 (Na) = 0.0120(1) Å2.

curated_sources_and_records.name: Luxembourgite
curated_sources_and_records.type_locality: Société Électrique de l'Our tunnel excavation dumps at Bivels (49°57'8" N, 6°10'41" E), northern Grand Duchy of Luxembourg
type_specimens: Cotype FD040 (Natural History Museum of Luxembourg / Musée National d'Histoire Naturelle, Luxembourg; portion used for EPMA)
Cotype 21302 (Laboratory of Mineralogy, University of Liège, Belgium; portion used for SCXRD)

primary_source.citation: Philippo S, Hatert F, Bruni Y, Vignola P, Sejkora J (2020) Luxembourgite, AgCuPbBi4Se8, a new mineral species from Bivels, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg. European Journal of Mineralogy 32:449-455

primary_source_discrepancies_documented: Section 4 (p. 450) prints the ideal composition of AgCuPbBi4Se8 as 'Ag 5.58, Cu 3.44, Pb 11.22, Bi 45.28, and Se 34.22 for a total of 100.00 wt %', where Ag 5.58 wt% is a digit transposition of the true stoichiometric value 5.84 wt% (107.8682 / 1846.3038 = 5.8424%), causing the five printed ideal values to sum to 99.74 wt%.

Calculated density is reported as 8.00 g/cm3 in the Abstract (p. 449), Section 3 (p. 450), and Table 6 (p. 454) from the chemical analysis and unit-cell parameters, whereas Table 3 (p. 452) reports Dcalc = 7.397 g/cm3.
Section 6 (p. 454) writes '(average M-O bond lengths = 2.544 Å in luxembourgite and 2.730 Å in litochlebite)', misprinting M-O for M-Se in an oxygen-free selenide.

curated_sources_and_records.name: Tancaite-(Ce)
curated_sources_and_records.type_locality: Oxidation zone of a sulfide ore vein within quartz veins cutting granite at Su Seinargiu, Sarroch (CA), Sardinia, Italy
type_specimens: Holotype 18911 (Natural History Museum, University of Pisa, Italy)

primary_source.citation: Bonaccorsi E, Orlandi P (2020) Tancaite-(Ce), ideally FeCe(MoO4)3*3H2O: description and average crystal structure. European Journal of Mineralogy 32:347-354

crystallography.space_group: Pm-3m (#221, average subcell) / R-3 (#148, real supercell)

primary_source_discrepancies_documented: The Abstract (p. 347) reports 'R1 = 0.038 for 192 unique reflections with I > 2sigma(I)', whereas Section 5 (p. 350) writes 'R1 = 0.038 for 200 unique reflections' and Table 4 (p. 352) reports 200 total independent reflections with Final R indices [I > 2sigma(I)] R1 = 0.0387, wR2 = 0.0792 and R indices (all data) R1 = 0.0424, wR2 = 0.0815.

The Table 4 caption (p. 352) states that the third column lists the trigonal R-3 unit cell 'as refined on the basis of X-ray powder diffraction data', whereas the values printed in that column (a = 19.2901(3), c = 47.2510(5) Å, V = 15226.9(7) Å3) are the single-crystal Bruker SMART BREEZE unit-cell parameters from Section 4 (p. 349), while the powder-diffraction refined R-3 cell in Section 4 and Table 3 (p. 350) is a = 19.305(1), c = 47.438(5) Å, V = 15311(3) Å3.
Calculated density is reported as 3.834 g/cm3 from the empirical formula (Abstract and Section 2, p. 348) vs 3.738 Mg/m3 (g/cm3) from the ideal formula CeFe(MoO4)3·3H2O in Table 4 (p. 352).

curated_sources_and_records.name: Argentotennantite-(Fe)
curated_sources_and_records.type_locality: Central part of the San Genaro mine (13°11'37" S, 75°08'57" W; 4750-5000 m a.s.l.), Castrovirreyna Province, Huancavelica, Peru
type_specimens: Holotype P1P 52/2023 (Department of Mineralogy and Petrology, National Museum in Prague, Czech Republic; polished section)
Holotype fragment 20070 (Museo di Storia Naturale of the Università di Pisa, Calci, Italy; grain used for single-crystal X-ray diffraction)

primary_source.citation: Sejkora J, Velebil D, Biagioni C, Dolníček Z, Hyršl J (2026) Argentotennantite-(Fe), Ag6(Cu4Fe2)As4S13, a new member of the tetrahedrite group from the San Genaro mine, Peru: occurrence and crystal structure. European Journal of Mineralogy 38:325-336

primary_source_discrepancies_documented: Section 4.1 (p. 329) reports the ideal composition of Ag6(Cu4Fe2)As4S13 as 'Cu 14.70, Ag 37.42, Fe 6.46, As 17.33, S 24.10, and total 100.00' wt%, where the five rounded constituent values sum to 100.01 wt%.

Section 4.2 (p. 332) states 'The tetrahedrally coordinated M(1) site has an average <M(1)–S> bond distance of 2.329 Å', whereas Table 5 (p. 330) and Table 8 (p. 333) report M(1)–S(1) x 4 = 2.328(3) Å.

Section 3.2 (p. 329) states that calculated powder X-ray diffraction data were obtained with 'PowderCell 2.3 (Kraus and Nolze, 1996)', whereas the Table 7 caption (p. 331) cites 'PowderCell 2.4 (Kraus and Nolze, 1996)'.

curated_sources_and_records.name: Badengzhuite
curated_sources_and_records.type_locality: Corundum grain separated from the Cr-11 podiform chromitite orebody (29°11' N, 92°18' E; 5300 m elevation), Kangjinla district, Luobusa ophiolite, Tibet, China
type_specimens: Holotype M13817 and FIB foil no. 5358 (Chinese Geological Museum, Xicheng District, Beijing, China)

primary_source.citation: Xiong F, Xu X, Mugnaioli E, Gemmi M, Wirth R, Grew ES, Robinson PT, Yang J (2020) Two new minerals, badengzhuite, TiP, and zhiqinite, TiSi2, from the Cr-11 chromitite orebody, Luobusa ophiolite, Tibet, China: is this evidence for super-reduced mantle-derived fluids? European Journal of Mineralogy 32:557-574

primary_source_discrepancies_documented: The Abstract (p. 557) reports the 3D ED unit cell of badengzhuite as 'a = 3.49(7) Å, c = 11.70(23) Å, V = 124(4) Å3', whereas Section 5.4 (p. 566) rounds c to 'c = 11.7(2) Å'.

Table 2 (p. 563) prints the average atomic percentages of the two EDX analyses (426: P 50.17, Ti 49.83 at.%; 427: P 47.86, Ti 52.14 at.%) as P 49.02 and Ti 50.99 at.% with 'Sum 100', where rounding both 49.015 and 50.985 upward yields an arithmetic sum of 100.01 at.%.
